## Goal

A healthy, reproducible R project. We open the `.Rproj`, restore the
environment with `renv`, and load the clinical data with stable, project-relative
paths (`here`) and a format-agnostic reader (`rio`).

<!--
Nota docente (IT): questo step è una DEMO (~10 min). Mostriamo l'ambiente sano:
`renv::restore()` è già stato fatto, la cartella ha il suo `.here` sentinel
così `here::here()` ancora alla cartella dello step (non alla root del workshop).
Il dato grezzo (`heart_failure.csv`, 299 righe × 13 colonne) vive in `data-raw/`.
-->

## Load the clinical data

We work with the **heart-failure clinical records** (Chicco & Jurman 2020): 299
patients followed after a heart-failure episode, with the outcome `DEATH_EVENT`.
The table was exported once to `data-raw/heart_failure.csv`.

```{r setup}
#| code-fold: false
library(here)
library(rio)

hf_raw <- import(here("data-raw", "heart_failure.csv"), setclass = "tibble")
dim(hf_raw)
```

The raw table has 299 rows and 13 columns — twelve clinical fields plus the
outcome. In the next step we shape it into the tidy tibble we model, and meet our
first data-hygiene decision (one of those columns must go).
